churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, dynamic opt-out, and config are each centralized in one place, so a framework upgrade touches few files — but the API boundary is typed as any throughout, so upstream schema changes surface as runtime breakage rather than compile errors.

findings.issue: Cache Components (cacheComponents + partialPrefetching) not enabled; the app runs on the previous caching model (fetch cache:'no-store' in app/src/lib/api.ts:29 plus a hand-rolled TTL cache) even though current Next 16 docs describe Cache Components as the default for new apps and say both flags will be forced in the next major release.
findings.suggestion: Enable cacheComponents/partialPrefetching and replace the custom TTL cache with 'use cache' + cacheLife; the data layer is already centralized in lib/api.ts, so the migration is contained.

findings.issue: API responses are typed as any (api<T = any>, apiOrNull<T = any>) and pages consume any-typed fields (app/src/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:58,102-111; app/src/app/abilities/[name]/page.tsx:24-30; app/src/app/types/[name]/page.tsx:37), so an upstream schema change fails at runtime instead of compile time.
findings.suggestion: Define response interfaces (even minimal ones) at the api.ts boundary and type the loaders' return values.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled TTL/LRU cache duplicates a capability the framework now owns; it works and is contained, but it's code to delete when the caching model moves.
findings.suggestion: Keep the module as the seam and swap its internals for framework caching rather than growing the custom cache.

findings.issue: Manual modifier-key and mouse-button checks on plain <a> elements re-implement next/link's navigation semantics; they can drift from framework behavior (e.g. prefetch, focus handling).
findings.suggestion: Use next/link with router state or Link's onClick for the intercept, keeping only the pushState fallback.

findings.issue: A non-404 API failure throws out of every server page with no error.tsx boundary, so a transient upstream 500 renders an unhandled error page.
findings.suggestion: Add an app/error.tsx (and/or catch in the data layer) to degrade gracefully.

findings.issue: The full 1,025-entry index (with per-entry type and generation arrays) is serialized into a client component's props on every request of /.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for the dataset size; if it grows, move filtering server-side or hold only ids client-side and derive display data on demand.

summary: A deliberately lean, platform-first App Router app on the current Next 16/React 19 generation, with data access and configuration each funneled through a single module so framework upgrades stay cheap. Its main forward-looking miss is staying on the previous caching model (explicit no-store fetches plus a hand-rolled TTL cache) rather than Cache Components, which current docs treat as the default heading into the next major. The other notable gap is untyped any responses at the API boundary, which pushes upstream schema churn from compile time to runtime.

apis.replacement: under Cache Components, dynamic is the default and 'use cache' marks cached work
